title: Literature and Composition Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of literary elements, character analysis, writing, poetry, and research skills!

questions.question: Which literary element describes WHERE and WHEN a story takes place?
questions.explanation: The setting is where and when the story takes place — the time and location of the events.

questions.question: A character who changes during a story is called a:
questions.explanation: A dynamic character is one who changes or grows during the story, like Saul becoming Paul.

questions.question: What are the three parts of an expository paragraph?
options: Topic sentence, supporting sentences, concluding sentence
questions.explanation: An expository paragraph has a topic sentence (main idea), supporting sentences (details), and a concluding sentence.

questions.question: Which type of writing tells a story?
questions.explanation: Narrative writing tells a story, whether true (personal narrative) or fictional.

questions.question: 'God is my rock' is an example of which poetic device?
questions.explanation: A metaphor says one thing IS another. 'God is my rock' compares God to a rock without using 'like' or 'as.'

questions.question: How many syllables does a haiku have in its three lines?
questions.explanation: A haiku has three lines with 5 syllables, 7 syllables, and 5 syllables.

questions.question: What is the MAIN problem or struggle in a story called?
questions.explanation: The conflict is the main problem or struggle that the characters face, which drives the story forward.

questions.question: When doing research, why should you write notes in your own words?
options: To make your handwriting look nice
To avoid copying and to show you understand the material
Because note cards are too small for full sentences
questions.explanation: Writing notes in your own words helps you understand the material and avoids copying someone else's work.
